note: Node class adds ONE base field `node_class` (string, 'CSS class(es)') to every node via hook_entity_base_field_info(), shows it in a 'Node Class settings' group on the node form (hook_form_node_form_alter), and appends the stored value to the rendered node's attributes.class via hook_preprocess_node(). No settings form (configure=null), no permission, no config entity/schema. All medium/hard cases are grounded in that real base field: introspection reads back the node_class value on a known node; execution sets node_class on a node and verifies it on the live entity.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal 11 site with the node_class module enabled, an editor wants to add a CSS class to a single node. Where do they enter it and where is that value stored on the node?
evals.expected_output: node_class adds a base field named node_class ('CSS class(es)') to all nodes. On the node add/edit form it appears in a collapsible 'Node Class settings' group in the advanced sidebar. The value is stored as ordinary node field content (the node_class base field), per node/revision; there is no admin settings page (configure=null).

evals.prompt: How does the node_class module actually get the class an editor typed onto the rendered node's HTML? Name the hook and the render variable it modifies.
evals.expected_output: node_class_preprocess_node() reads $entity->get('node_class') and appends the value to $variables['attributes']['class'], which the node template prints on the wrapping <article> element (e.g. <article{{ attributes }}>). It applies to every view mode.

evals.prompt: With node_class enabled, do I need to add a field to each content type under Manage fields to use it? Explain why or why not.
evals.expected_output: No. node_class is declared as a base field via hook_entity_base_field_info() on the node entity type, so the node_class field exists automatically on every content type without any per-bundle 'Manage fields' setup.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is an Article node whose title is exactly 'node_class introspection target'. Using node_class, read the CSS class that has been assigned to that node and report its value.
evals.expected_output: The node's node_class base field holds 'nc-known-42' (readable via $node->get('node_class')->value).

evals.prompt: This site has two Article nodes titled 'node_class candidate A' and 'node_class candidate B'. Exactly one of them has a CSS class set via node_class. Inspect the live nodes and state which title has a node_class value and what it is.
evals.expected_output: 'node_class candidate B' has the node_class value 'nc-b-highlight'; 'node_class candidate A' has an empty node_class field.

evals.prompt: On this site there is an Article node titled 'node_class execution target'. Using the node_class module's field, set that node's CSS class to exactly `nc-hero` and save the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: The node's node_class base field is set to 'nc-hero' ($node->set('node_class','nc-hero')->save()), so the rendered node carries the nc-hero class.

evals.prompt: Create a new Article node titled 'node_class new post' and, using node_class, give it the CSS class `nc-created` in the same step. Save it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A published Article node 'node_class new post' exists whose node_class base field equals 'nc-created'.
